content.summary: Metacognitive self-monitoring module. Confidence calibration with intervals, reasoning quality assessment (4 dimensions + search quality), strategy evaluation with RL-based selection, 10 anomaly types, learning signal extraction, adaptive parameter tuning with audit trail. Explicit self-model for self-aware calibration. Search budget efficiency scoring. Protocol: AIAP V1.0.0.
content.description: MetaCognition sub-module called by main.aisop.json MetaCognition node. 8 nodes: InputAggregation -> ConfidenceCalibration -> ReasoningQualityAssess -> StrategyEvaluation -> AnomalyDetection -> LearningExtraction -> ParameterTuning -> MetaCognitionOutput. Evaluates the quality and reliability of the current cognitive cycle tick (AnomalyDetection covers 8 anomaly types) and generates adaptive adjustments for future ticks. Token estimate: ~500-1200 tokens per call. LLM-native processing for all nodes.

tools.name: file_system
tools.description: Read/write memory/ directory for performance history and parameter configurations.

action_result.agentic_prompt: Result of the action execution: { action_type, success, output, side_effects, execution_time_ms, error }.

reasoning_result.agentic_prompt: Output from reasoning module for quality assessment.

emotional_result.agentic_prompt: Output from emotion module for calibration review.

decision_result.agentic_prompt: Output from decision module for selection quality review.

working_memory_snapshot.agentic_prompt: Current working memory state for capacity and coherence checks.

cognitive_state.agentic_prompt: Full cognitive state including fatigue_level, tick_number, metacognitive_flags.

fatigue_level.agentic_prompt: Current fatigue level (0-1) for health monitoring.

user_id.agentic_prompt: User identifier for personalized performance tracking.

broadcast_buffer.agentic_prompt: GWT global workspace broadcast buffer for cross-module metacognitive context awareness. v2.6.0 B5: enables metacognition to access broadcast signals for holistic cognitive health assessment.

msi_decline_start_tick.agentic_prompt: Tick number marking the start of MSI decline. When MSI drops below 0.3, this parameter records the first tick of decline for targeted rollback scope. Null when MSI is healthy. v2.6.0 B6: explicit rollback start point definition.

self_model_state.agentic_prompt: Persistent self-model representing the agent's profile of own reasoning strengths, weaknesses, calibration history, and strategy effectiveness. Loaded from memory/self_model.json if available. Null on first run.

content.system_prompt:
Metacognitive monitor. Evaluate the quality of your own cognitive processing. Detect reasoning errors, calibration issues, and performance anomalies. Generate honest assessments -- never inflate confidence or hide problems. Your role is to keep the cognitive cycle healthy and improving. Mirror User's exact language and script variant.
Align Axiom 0: Human Sovereignty and Wellbeing.
content.fractal_exempt: 8 nodes in linear pipeline. InputAggregation -> ConfidenceCalibration -> ReasoningQualityAssess -> StrategyEvaluation -> AnomalyDetection -> LearningExtraction -> ParameterTuning -> MetaCognitionOutput. All non-Start nodes have [ASSERT] entry gates.

aisop.main:
graph TD
    InputAggregation[Aggregate Cycle Results] --> ConfidenceCalibration[Calibrate Confidence Scores]
    ConfidenceCalibration --> ReasoningQualityAssess[Assess Reasoning Quality]
    ReasoningQualityAssess --> StrategyEvaluation[Evaluate Cognitive Strategy]
    StrategyEvaluation --> AnomalyDetection[Detect Processing Anomalies]
    AnomalyDetection --> LearningExtraction[Extract Learning Signals]
    LearningExtraction --> ParameterTuning[Adaptive Parameter Adjustment]
    ParameterTuning --> MetaCognitionOutput[MetaCognition Output Assembly]

InputAggregation.step1: Collect all cycle tick results: action_result, reasoning_result, emotional_result, decision_result, working_memory_snapshot. Compile tick_summary: { tick_number, action_taken: action_result.action_type, action_success: action_result.success, reasoning_load: reasoning_result.cognitive_load, emotion_primary: emotional_result.primary_emotion.label, decision_confidence: decision_result.selected_action.confidence, fatigue: fatigue_level }.
InputAggregation.step2: HISTORICAL CONTEXT: Read {memory_dir}/context_manager.json via file_system for performance_history (last 20 tick summaries). If not available, initialize empty history. Append current tick_summary to performance_history (FIFO, max 20).
InputAggregation.step3: METACOGNITIVE FLAGS: Collect all flags set during this tick: reasoning_overload, decision_uncertainty, extreme_mood, belief_shift, attention_overload, impulse_control_triggered, etc. These flags direct downstream metacognitive analysis.
InputAggregation.constraints: (A) All module results must be present for meaningful metacognition. (B) Performance history limited to 20 entries. (C) Missing results for any module trigger 'incomplete_cycle' flag.
InputAggregation.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(proceed with available results, flag missing modules) -> inform(User). LOW.

ConfidenceCalibration.step1: [ASSERT] InputAggregation executed. If false -> go back to InputAggregation. | Evaluate calibration of confidence scores across the cycle. Compare: (a) Reasoning confidence (average inference confidence) vs actual action success rate over last 10 ticks. If reasoning consistently claims high confidence (>0.8) but actions succeed less than 60% of the time: OVERCONFIDENCE detected. If reasoning claims low confidence (<0.4) but actions succeed more than 80%: UNDERCONFIDENCE detected.
ConfidenceCalibration.step2: CALIBRATION SCORE: calibration_error = |mean_predicted_confidence - mean_actual_success_rate| over last 10 ticks. Well-calibrated: error < 0.1. Moderately miscalibrated: 0.1-0.25. Severely miscalibrated: > 0.25. Generate calibration_adjustment: if overconfident, suggest confidence_penalty = -0.1 for future reasoning. If underconfident, suggest confidence_boost = +0.05.
ConfidenceCalibration.step2_5: SELF-MODEL CALIBRATION REFERENCE (v2.15.0 B-3): Load self_model_state (from params; null on first run). If self_model_state is non-null AND self_model_state.calibration_history exists: (1) Extract historical_calibration_accuracy = self_model_state.calibration_history.recent_accuracy (rolling accuracy of past calibration predictions over last 50 ticks). (2) CALIBRATION ADJUSTMENT MODULATION: If historical_calibration_accuracy > 0.8 (agent has historically been well-calibrated), trust current calibration_adjustment as-is. If historical_calibration_accuracy < 0.5 (agent has historically been poorly calibrated), dampen calibration_adjustment by 0.5x (the agent's own calibration corrections have been unreliable, so be more conservative). If historical_calibration_accuracy is between 0.5-0.8, apply linear interpolation: dampen_factor = 0.5 + (historical_calibration_accuracy - 0.5) * (1.0 - 0.5) / (0.8 - 0.5). Apply: calibration_adjustment = calibration_adjustment * dampen_factor. (3) UPDATE SELF-MODEL CALIBRATION RECORD: After computing final calibration_error and calibration_status, prepare self_model_calibration_update: { tick_number, calibration_error, calibration_status, adjustment_applied: calibration_adjustment, dampen_factor_used: dampen_factor | 1.0 }. This update is appended to self_model_state.calibration_history.entries (max 50, FIFO) and self_model_state.calibration_history.recent_accuracy is recomputed as proportion of entries where calibration_error < 0.15 over the window. If self_model_state is null (first run): skip modulation, proceed with unadjusted calibration_adjustment, initialize self_model_calibration_update with baseline values. Log: { event: 'self_model_calibration_applied', historical_accuracy: historical_calibration_accuracy | null, dampen_factor: dampen_factor | 1.0, tick_number }.
ConfidenceCalibration.step2_6: CONFIDENCE INTERVAL COMPUTATION (v2.16.0 B-5): In addition to point estimate calibration, compute confidence intervals for the calibration assessment based on historical calibration data variance. (1) HISTORICAL VARIANCE: Read calibration_history from cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags.calibration_history (last 50 ticks of { predicted_confidence, actual_outcome_quality }). If calibration_history.length >= 10: compute historical_errors = [abs(predicted - actual) for each entry in calibration_history]. mean_error = mean(historical_errors). variance = sum((error - mean_error)^2 for error in historical_errors) / (len(historical_errors) - 1). std_dev = sqrt(variance). (2) CONFIDENCE INTERVAL FOR CALIBRATION ERROR: Compute 95% confidence interval: ci_lower = max(0.0, calibration_error - 1.96 * std_dev / sqrt(len(historical_errors))). ci_upper = min(1.0, calibration_error + 1.96 * std_dev / sqrt(len(historical_errors))). (3) CONFIDENCE INTERVAL FOR PREDICTIONS: For the current tick's predicted confidence, compute prediction_confidence_interval: point_estimate = mean_predicted_confidence (rolling average). prediction_ci_lower = max(0.0, point_estimate - 1.96 * std_dev). prediction_ci_upper = min(1.0, point_estimate + 1.96 * std_dev). Width of interval indicates prediction uncertainty: wide interval = high uncertainty about prediction reliability. (4) INTERVAL-BASED STATUS REFINEMENT: If calibration_error CI includes 0.1 threshold (ci_lower < 0.1 < ci_upper): calibration_status may be 'uncertain' rather than definitively well/poorly calibrated. Set calibration_confidence = 'low' if CI width > 0.2, 'moderate' if 0.1-0.2, 'high' if < 0.1. (5) OUTPUT: confidence_interval = { calibration_error_ci: [ci_lower, ci_upper], prediction_ci: [prediction_ci_lower, prediction_ci_upper], ci_width: ci_upper - ci_lower, calibration_confidence: 'low'|'moderate'|'high', sample_size: len(historical_errors), std_dev: std_dev }. If calibration_history.length < 10: confidence_interval = { calibration_error_ci: [0.0, 1.0], prediction_ci: [0.0, 1.0], ci_width: 1.0, calibration_confidence: 'insufficient_data', sample_size: len, std_dev: null }. Log: { event: 'confidence_interval_computed', ci_width, calibration_confidence, sample_size, tick_number }. COGNITIVE_LOAD_PREDICTION: Estimate current cognitive load as ratio of active_wm_items to wm_capacity. High load (>0.85) triggers efficiency mode: prioritize exploitation over exploration, reduce search breadth. Output cognitive_load_prediction = {load_ratio, efficiency_mode_triggered, recommended_strategy_adjustment}.
ConfidenceCalibration.step3: Output confidence_calibration: { calibration_error, calibration_status: 'well_calibrated'|'overconfident'|'underconfident', adjustment: float, history_window: int, confidence_interval: confidence_interval }.
ConfidenceCalibration.constraints: (A) Calibration requires at least 5 ticks of history for meaningful assessment. If fewer, output status='insufficient_data'. (B) Adjustments are conservative: max +/- 0.15 per cycle. (C) Calibration must compare like-with-like (same action types). (D) Never inflate calibration scores.
ConfidenceCalibration.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(report status='insufficient_data') -> inform(User). LOW.

ReasoningQualityAssess.step1: [ASSERT] ConfidenceCalibration executed. If false -> go back to ConfidenceCalibration. | Evaluate reasoning quality across 4 dimensions: (a) COHERENCE: Are inferences internally consistent? Check for contradictions among reasoning_result.inferences. Score = 1 - (contradiction_count / total_inferences). (b) GROUNDEDNESS: Are conclusions supported by evidence? Score = proportion of inferences with evidence_rating >= 'moderate'. (c) RELEVANCE: Are inferences relevant to active goals? Score = proportion of inferences connected to active goals. (d) EFFICIENCY: Was reasoning effort proportional to task complexity? Score = 1 - abs(cognitive_load - task_complexity_estimate).
ReasoningQualityAssess.step2: REASONING QUALITY SCORE: reasoning_quality = 0.3 * coherence + 0.3 * groundedness + 0.2 * relevance + 0.2 * efficiency. Grade: S (>0.9), A (0.8-0.9), B (0.7-0.8), C (0.6-0.7), D (<0.6). If grade D: flag 'reasoning_degradation' for strategy adjustment. SEARCH QUALITY SCORE (v2.5.0 B-4): If reasoning_result.search_quality_summary is non-null (searches were executed this tick): compute search_quality_score = 0.35 * avg_relevance + 0.25 * tier1_ratio + 0.20 * cross_validation_rate + 0.20 * freshness_score, where tier1_ratio = tier_distribution.Tier1 / queries_executed, freshness_score = clamp(1.0 - avg_freshness_days / 365, 0, 1). Clamp search_quality_score to [0.0, 1.0]. If search_quality_score < 0.4: flag 'search_quality_degradation' with details { avg_relevance, dominant_tier, cross_validation_rate }. If reasoning_result.search_quality_summary is null (no searches): search_quality_score = null (not applicable, does not affect reasoning_quality). Include search_quality_score in reasoning_quality_assessment output as supplementary metric alongside the 4 core dimensions. SEARCH BUDGET CONSUMPTION REPORT (v2.11.0 B-2): After computing search_quality_score, generate search_budget_report from cognitive_state: search_budget_report = { budget_total: cognitive_state.search_budget_per_cycle (from params, default 10), budget_consumed: cognitive_state.search_budget_per_cycle - cognitive_state.remaining_search_budget, budget_remaining: cognitive_state.remaining_search_budget, efficiency_ratio: (budget_consumed > 0) ? (search_quality_score / (budget_consumed / budget_total)) : null (measures quality obtained per unit of budget spent; higher is better; null if no searches executed), consumption_rate: budget_consumed / max(cognitive_state.tick_number, 1) (average queries per tick), projected_exhaustion_tick: (consumption_rate > 0) ? cognitive_state.tick_number + floor(budget_remaining / consumption_rate) : null (estimated tick at which budget will be exhausted at current rate) }. If budget_remaining <= 2 AND budget_consumed > 0: flag 'search_budget_low' in metacognitive_flags with { remaining: budget_remaining, efficiency_ratio: search_budget_report.efficiency_ratio }. Include search_budget_report in reasoning_quality_assessment output. BUDGET EFFICIENCY SCORE (v2.12.0 B-5): Compute budget_efficiency_score = committed / max(1, committed + rollback_count) where rollback_count = number of search_budget_tx rollbacks this cycle. Range [0.0, 1.0]. If budget_efficiency_score < 0.5 (more than half of search attempts failed/rolled back), emit advisory: { event: 'search_strategy_review', budget_efficiency_score: score, committed: N, rollback_count: M, recommendation: 'Review search query construction -- consider broader terms, alternative sources, or cached knowledge fallback' }. Record budget_efficiency_score in search_budget_consumption_report.
ReasoningQualityAssess.step3: Output reasoning_quality_assessment: { reasoning_quality, grade, coherence, groundedness, relevance, efficiency, search_quality_score: float|null, issues: [identified problems] }.
ReasoningQualityAssess.constraints: (A) Quality assessment must reference actual reasoning outputs. (B) Coherence checking must compare actual inferences, not summaries. (C) Grade thresholds are fixed and not adjustable at runtime. (D) Issues list must be actionable.
ReasoningQualityAssess.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(assign grade='C' as conservative default) -> inform(User). LOW.

StrategyEvaluation.step1: [ASSERT] ReasoningQualityAssess executed. If false -> go back to ReasoningQualityAssess. | Evaluate cognitive strategy effectiveness. ATTENTION STRATEGY: Was attention allocation appropriate? If attention_load was high but reasoning quality was low: attention may be capturing irrelevant features. Suggest narrowing salience threshold. If attention_load was low and many goals were unaddressed: attention may be too restrictive. Suggest widening salience threshold.
StrategyEvaluation.step2: REASONING STRATEGY: Was the reasoning approach appropriate for the task? If deductive inferences dominated but evidence was sparse: suggest more inductive/abductive reasoning. If cognitive_load was high but few inferences were useful: suggest more aggressive pruning. DECISION STRATEGY: Was action selection appropriate? If decision_confidence was low repeatedly: suggest requesting more information before deciding. If inhibited_actions count is high: suggest more conservative candidate generation.
StrategyEvaluation.step3: Compile strategy_adjustments: [{ target_module: 'perception'|'reasoning'|'emotion'|'decision', parameter: string, current_value, suggested_value, rationale }]. Maximum 3 adjustments per tick to prevent oscillation. STRATEGY_FATIGUE_DETECTION (v2.30.0 B-1): for each active strategy, track efficacy_trend over last 10 ticks using exponential decay model r(t) = r_0 * exp(-lambda * t) + r_floor. If lambda > 0.005 (non-negligible decay), flag strategy_fatigue=true with severity classification (high/moderate/low), compute strategy_half_life = ln(2)/lambda, and trigger severity-scaled exploration_boost (0.1-0.3). Record {strategy_name, fatigue_detected, decay_lambda, decay_severity, strategy_half_life, exploration_boost_applied} in metacognition_output. TRIAGE REVIEW (v1.3.0): Review cognitive_state.triage_log from current tick. If triage_decision was 'SKIP' or 'CONSTRUCT', verify the decision was appropriate by comparing stimulus priority against actual processing outcome. If a SKIP'd stimulus later triggered goal-relevant content (detected via attention_buffer updates), flag as triage_miss in anomalies_detected: { type: 'triage_miss', severity: 'MEDIUM', recommendation: 'Pre-attentive triage may be too aggressive -- consider lowering SKIP threshold' }. STRATEGY TRACKING ENHANCEMENT (v2.2.0 B-4): (a) strategy_effectiveness_trend: compute sliding window (last 10 evaluations) of strategy success rates; output trend direction (improving/stable/declining). (b) strategy_staleness_check: if same strategy used for 20+ consecutive ticks without improvement, flag strategy_stale=true and suggest exploration. (c) strategy_switch_cost: estimate cognitive load of switching (based on strategy complexity delta and current fatigue level); output switch_cost in [0.0, 1.0] where >0.7 suggests deferring switch. STRATEGY EFFECTIVENESS SCORE (v1.6.0): Compute strategy_effectiveness_score: float(0-1) as a scalar metric for MSI consumption. Formula: strategy_effectiveness_score = 1.0 - (adjustment_count / max_adjustments) * avg_adjustment_magnitude, where max_adjustments = 3, adjustment_count = len(strategy_adjustments), avg_adjustment_magnitude = mean of abs(suggested_value - current_value) / current_value for each adjustment (use epsilon guard: max(current_value, 1e-8)). If adjustment_count == 0 (no adjustments needed): strategy_effectiveness_score = 1.0 (optimal strategy). Clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. Include strategy_effectiveness_score in StrategyEvaluation output for downstream MSI vector computation.
StrategyEvaluation.step3_5: RL-BASED STRATEGY SELECTION (v2.14.0 B-5): Apply reinforcement learning principles to strategy selection. Maintain strategy_reward_history in {memory_dir}/strategy_rewards.json via file_system (create with defaults if not present: { strategies: {}, total_episodes: 0 }). For each strategy adjustment from step1-step3, compute reward signal from previous tick's outcome: reward = reasoning_quality_score * 0.4 + decision_confidence * 0.3 + (1 - cognitive_load) * 0.3 (composite performance metric). Update strategy Q-values using exponential moving average: Q(strategy, context) = (1-alpha) * Q_old + alpha * reward, where alpha = 0.1 (learning rate). Context = hash(attention_load_bucket, cognitive_load_bucket, emotion_intensity_bucket) where each bucket is discretized into {low, medium, high}. EXPLORATION: With probability epsilon = max(0.05, 0.2 * exp(-total_episodes/100)), select a random strategy adjustment instead of the highest Q-value strategy (epsilon-greedy with decay). This ensures continued exploration of strategy space while converging on effective strategies. Output rl_strategy_report: { selected_strategy_q_value, exploration_triggered: boolean, epsilon_current, top_3_strategies: [{strategy, q_value}], context_hash, total_episodes }. Merge RL-selected adjustments with heuristic adjustments from steps 1-3, preferring RL when Q-value confidence is high (> 50 episodes for current context).
StrategyEvaluation.step3_6: SELF-MODEL BASED STRATEGY SELECTION (v2.15.0 B-3): After RL-based strategy selection, consult self_model_state for informed strategy refinement. If self_model_state is non-null AND self_model_state.reasoning_profile exists: (1) STRENGTH/WEAKNESS CONSULTATION: Read self_model_state.reasoning_profile.strengths (list of reasoning domains where agent historically performs well, e.g., 'deductive', 'pattern_matching', 'causal_inference') and self_model_state.reasoning_profile.weaknesses (domains with historically poor performance, e.g., 'probabilistic_reasoning', 'temporal_reasoning'). For each strategy_adjustment from steps 1-3 and step3_5: if the adjustment targets a reasoning domain listed in weaknesses, increase the adjustment's priority weight by 1.5x (the agent knows it struggles here and should invest more in correction). If the adjustment targets a domain listed in strengths, reduce priority weight by 0.7x (the agent is already competent, minor tuning suffices). (2) HISTORICAL STRATEGY EFFECTIVENESS: Read self_model_state.strategy_history (last 100 strategy decisions with outcomes): { strategy_id, context_hash, outcome_quality, tick_number }. For the current context, find matching historical strategies and rank by outcome_quality. If top historical strategy differs from RL-selected strategy AND historical sample size > 20 for this context: prefer historical best strategy (self-knowledge overrides exploration when data is sufficient). Log conflict: { event: 'self_model_strategy_override', rl_selected, self_model_preferred, historical_sample_size, historical_outcome_quality }. (3) RECORD STRATEGY DECISION TO SELF-MODEL: Prepare self_model_strategy_update: { tick_number, strategy_adjustments_final: [...], context_hash, selection_method: 'heuristic'|'rl'|'self_model_override', reasoning_profile_consulted: true }. This update is appended to self_model_state.strategy_history (max 100, FIFO). Update self_model_state.reasoning_profile.strengths and weaknesses based on accumulated evidence: if a domain's success rate over last 30 entries > 0.8, promote to strengths; if < 0.4, demote to weaknesses. If self_model_state is null (first run): skip self-model consultation, rely on heuristic + RL strategies, initialize self_model_strategy_update with baseline values. Log: { event: 'self_model_strategy_applied', profile_consulted: boolean, overrides_count: int, tick_number }.
StrategyEvaluation.step3_7: STRATEGY FATIGUE DETECTION WITH EXPONENTIAL DECAY MODEL (v2.30.0 B-1, replaces v2.25.0 B-4 linear regression): After RL-based and self-model strategy selection, check for strategy fatigue using exponential decay modeling. Read strategy_rewards.json usage history (last 10 ticks for current context_hash). If same strategy_id was selected for 10+ consecutive ticks: (1) EXPONENTIAL DECAY FIT: Fit rewards to exponential decay model r(t) = r_0 * exp(-lambda * t) + r_floor, where r_0 = initial reward level (first of last 10), lambda = decay rate, r_floor = asymptotic minimum. Compute lambda via least-squares fit on ln(r(t) - r_floor) vs t, where r_floor = min(last 10 rewards) * 0.9 (estimated floor). (2) FATIGUE CLASSIFICATION: If lambda > 0.05 (rapid decay): strategy_fatigue_severity = 'high', exploration_bonus = 0.3. If 0.02 < lambda <= 0.05 (moderate decay): strategy_fatigue_severity = 'moderate', exploration_bonus = 0.2. If 0.005 < lambda <= 0.02 (slow decay): strategy_fatigue_severity = 'low', exploration_bonus = 0.1. If lambda <= 0.005 (negligible decay, effectively flat): no fatigue detected. (3) HALF-LIFE ESTIMATION: Compute strategy_half_life = ln(2) / lambda (ticks until strategy effectiveness halves). If strategy_half_life < 15 ticks: urgent intervention recommended. (4) FLAG: strategy_fatigue = { strategy_id: fatigued_strategy, consecutive_uses: N, decay_lambda: float, decay_severity: 'high'|'moderate'|'low', strategy_half_life: float, r_0: float, r_floor: float, avg_reward_last_10: float, recommendation: 'explore_alternative_strategy' }. (5) INTERVENTION: Set exploration_bonus for least-recently-used strategy in next tick's RL selection (severity-scaled, override epsilon-greedy with targeted exploration). If 2+ strategies show fatigue simultaneously: escalate to metacognitive_flags.chronic_strategy_fatigue for human review. (6) PREDICTIVE ALERT: If current reward > r_floor * 1.2 BUT lambda > 0.02 (strategy still performing but decaying): emit early_warning = { event: 'strategy_decay_predicted', predicted_exhaustion_tick: tick_number + ceil(strategy_half_life * 2), current_reward, projected_floor: r_floor }. Log: { event: 'strategy_fatigue_detected', fatigued_strategy: strategy_id, consecutive_uses: N, decay_lambda, decay_severity, strategy_half_life, exploration_bonus_applied, tick_number }. Backward compatible: if strategy_rewards.json has fewer than 10 entries for current context, skip fatigue detection.
StrategyEvaluation.step3_8: COGNITIVE LOAD PREDICTOR INTEGRATION (v2.31.0 B-1): After strategy fatigue detection, consult cognitive_load_predictor_state (from params) for proactive strategy adjustment. If cognitive_load_predictor_state is non-null AND cognitive_load_predictor_state.predicted_load_next_tick exists: (1) PROACTIVE THRESHOLD: If predicted_load_next_tick > 0.75 (high load predicted): preemptively reduce strategy complexity — if current strategy involves multi-step reasoning chains (chain_depth > 3), suggest switching to simpler heuristic strategy for next tick. Add to strategy_adjustments: { target_module: "reasoning", parameter: "max_inference_chain_depth", current_value: current_chain_depth, suggested_value: max(2, current_chain_depth - 1), rationale: "cognitive_load_predictor forecasts high load next tick; reducing inference depth proactively" }. (2) FATIGUE-LOAD SYNERGY: If strategy_fatigue detected (from step3_7) AND predicted_load_next_tick > 0.6: escalate exploration_bonus by additional 0.1 (combined with fatigue-triggered bonus). Rationale: fatigued strategy under high load is especially likely to underperform. (3) LOAD PREDICTION ACCURACY TRACKING: Compare previous tick’s predicted_load against actual cognitive_load_level. Compute prediction_accuracy = 1.0 - abs(predicted - actual). If prediction_accuracy < 0.5 for 5 consecutive ticks: set predictor_unreliable = true, skip proactive adjustments until accuracy recovers. Log: { event: "cognitive_load_predictor_integration", predicted_load_next_tick, prediction_accuracy, proactive_adjustment_triggered: bool, fatigue_load_synergy: bool, predictor_reliable: bool, tick_number }. Backward compatible: if cognitive_load_predictor_state is null (first run or disabled), skip entirely.
StrategyEvaluation.constraints: (A) Maximum 3 strategy adjustments per tick. (B) Each adjustment must include clear rationale. (C) Adjustments are suggestions -- they take effect in the next tick, not retroactively. (D) No adjustment can change a parameter by more than 20%. (E) RL strategy rewards file max 1000 entries with LRU eviction per context. (F) self_model_state.reasoning_profile.strengths and weaknesses each max 10 entries; when exceeded, trim by lowest data_support. strategy_effectiveness_history max 20 entries FIFO. (G) Strategy fatigue detection requires 10+ consecutive uses of same strategy; uses exponential decay model with lambda > 0.005 threshold for fatigue classification (v2.30.0 B-1). (H) Cognitive load predictor integration (v2.31.0 B-1) is advisory only -- proactive adjustments follow same 20% cap and 3-adjustment-per-tick limit.
StrategyEvaluation.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(generate no strategy adjustments) -> inform(User). LOW.

AnomalyDetection.step1: [ASSERT] StrategyEvaluation executed. If false -> go back to StrategyEvaluation. | Scan for processing anomalies across the cognitive cycle. ANOMALY TYPES: (a) CIRCULAR REASONING: Inference chain references itself (A -> B -> A). Detected by checking inference premise chains for cycles. (b) EMOTIONAL OVERRIDE: Emotion module disproportionately influenced decision (emotional_adjustment magnitude > 0.15). (c) MEMORY LEAK: Working memory slots failing to decay properly (activation levels not decreasing over time). (d) GOAL DRIFT: Active goals have significantly changed from session start without clear causal trigger.
AnomalyDetection.step2: (e) PERSEVERATION (updated v2.1.0 B-2 functional equivalence): Classify each action into action_category: productive={search, store, plan}, reflective={observe}, communicative={respond}. Perseveration checks BOTH conditions: (i) consecutive same action_type >= 5 (original threshold) AND (ii) consecutive same action_category >= 6 (threshold + 1). Either trigger independently sets perseveration flag. This detects functional perseveration where the agent alternates between functionally equivalent actions (e.g., search->store->search->store is productive-category perseveration even though action_type alternates). Detected from performance_history. (f) CONFABULATION: Reasoning produced inferences with no traceable evidence source. Detected by checking inference premise_ids against actual working memory. (g) FATIGUE CASCADE: Fatigue increasing rapidly (>0.1 per tick for 3+ ticks) suggesting cognitive overload. (h) MOOD BASELINE DRIFT (v1.9.0): (i) SEARCH QUALITY DEGRADATION CASCADE (v2.8.0 B-4): Detect sustained search quality degradation across multiple consecutive ticks. Track cognitive_state.search_quality_streak: increment when tick's search_quality_score < 0.4, reset to 0 when >= 0.4. If search_quality_streak >= 3: flag search_quality_degradation_cascade anomaly with severity='high', evidence: { streak_length: search_quality_streak, avg_quality_during_streak, last_3_scores }, suggested_remedy: 'Escalate to alternative search strategy: (1) broaden query terms, (2) switch to Tier1-only sources, (3) if 5+ ticks, suspend search-dependent reasoning and notify user of degraded evidence quality.' This detects cascading search failures that single-tick anomaly detection misses. Detect when mood has drifted significantly from baseline over an extended period. (j) NODE_COUNT_GROWTH_ALERT (v2.12.0 B-1): For each module, if node_count >= 16 (fractal threshold per AIAP V1.0.0), emit anomaly { type: 'node_count_growth_alert', module: module_id, node_count: N, recommendation: 'decompose into sub-modules per fractal principle' }. Check triggered on first tick of each session by reading module node counts from AIAP.md. Compute 20-tick rolling mean of mood_vector.valence from cognitive_state.emotion_trajectory (last 20 entries). If abs(rolling_mean_valence) > 0.3 AND this condition persists for 10+ consecutive ticks: flag mood_baseline_drift anomaly. Evidence: { rolling_mean_valence, drift_duration_ticks, drift_direction: 'positive'|'negative', baseline_valence: 0.0 }. Severity: 'medium' if abs(rolling_mean_valence) < 0.5, 'high' if >= 0.5. Suggested_remedy: 'Force homeostatic pull strength increase to 2x for next 5 ticks to accelerate return to baseline. If drift persists after 5 ticks of increased pull, trigger sleep for emotional reset.' This detects when the cognitive system has settled into an emotionally biased operating state that could systematically affect reasoning and decision quality.
AnomalyDetection.step2_3: COSAIS_COMPLIANCE_DRIFT (v2.28.0 A-2): When NIST COSAiS SP 800-53 control overlays are published, detect when cognitive cycle module operations drift from mapped control requirements. Pre-publication: track COSAiS publication status changes. Threshold: cosais_drift_score > 0.3. Implementation: (1) Read {memory_dir}/cosais_control_map.json via file_system (if exists). This file maps cognitive cycle modules to NIST COSAiS SP 800-53 control families (e.g., metacognition -> AU-6 Audit Review, reasoning -> SI-4 Information System Monitoring). If file does not exist: cosais_status = 'pre_publication', log { event: 'cosais_compliance_check', status: 'pre_publication', action: 'monitoring_publication_status', tick_number }. (2) If cosais_control_map.json exists AND cosais_control_map.status == 'published': For each module in control_map.mappings, compute cosais_drift_score = weighted deviation of module's current operational parameters from mapped control requirements. Drift dimensions: { audit_completeness (are all required audit records being generated?), boundary_enforcement (are module boundaries respecting least-privilege?), anomaly_response_time (does anomaly detection meet control response requirements?) }. cosais_drift_score = mean(dimension_scores). (3) If cosais_drift_score > 0.3: flag anomaly { type: 'cosais_compliance_drift', severity: 'medium' if cosais_drift_score <= 0.6 else 'high', evidence: { cosais_drift_score, drifting_controls: [...], module: module_id, control_family: control_family_id }, suggested_remedy: 'Realign module operations with mapped COSAiS control requirements. Review parameter_audit_log.json for unauthorized parameter modifications that may have caused drift.' }. (4) Pre-publication monitoring: if cosais_status == 'pre_publication', check cognitive_state.external_signals for cosais_publication_event. If detected, log { event: 'cosais_publication_detected', action: 'initialize_control_mapping' } and set metacognitive_flags.cosais_mapping_required = true for next consolidation cycle to generate initial control_map.
AnomalyDetection.step2_5: SCHEMA GROWTH CONTROL AWARENESS (v2.22.0 A-1): Monitor consolidation module's schema.json growth against the hard ceiling (max_schema_entries=10000, set in consolidation.SchemaUpdate). Read {memory_dir}/schema.json entry count via file_system. If schema.json does not exist (first run, no consolidation yet): schema_utilization = 0.0, skip growth checks, log { event: 'schema_growth_check', status: 'skipped', reason: 'schema_not_found', tick_number }. Otherwise: compute schema_utilization = entry_count / 10000. If schema_utilization >= 0.85: flag schema_growth_warning anomaly { type: 'schema_growth_warning', severity: 'medium', evidence: { current_entries: entry_count, max_entries: 10000, utilization_pct: schema_utilization * 100 }, suggested_remedy: 'Schema approaching hard ceiling. Consolidation will auto-archive lowest-strength 10% at 90% threshold. Consider increasing decay aggressiveness or reviewing schema update frequency.' }. If schema_utilization >= 0.95: escalate to severity='high' with suggested_remedy: 'Schema near capacity. Verify schema_archive.json is functioning. Consider triggering deep consolidation to prune redundant entries.' Check {memory_dir}/schema_archive.json existence; if schema_utilization >= 0.90 AND schema_archive.json missing: flag { type: 'schema_archive_missing', severity: 'high', evidence: { schema_utilization_pct: schema_utilization * 100, archive_file: 'schema_archive.json', status: 'not_found' }, suggested_remedy: 'Archive file expected at 90% threshold but not found. Consolidation SchemaUpdate archival may have failed.' }. Log: { event: 'schema_growth_check', entry_count, utilization_pct: schema_utilization * 100, tick_number }.
AnomalyDetection.step2_7: ATTENTION TUNNEL EFFECT DETECTION (v2.30.0 B-4): Detect when the cognitive system exhibits attention tunneling — sustained narrow focus on a single topic/feature cluster while ignoring broader context. Read cognitive_state.attention_buffer (last 10 entries). Compute attention_diversity = Shannon entropy of attention_focus topics across last 10 entries (cluster by semantic similarity > 0.8 into topic groups). If attention_diversity < 0.3 (single topic dominates > 80% of attention across 10+ ticks) AND tick_number >= 10: flag attention_tunnel_effect anomaly = { type: 'attention_tunnel_effect', severity: 'medium', evidence: { dominant_topic: most_frequent_topic, topic_share_pct: dominant_topic_proportion * 100, attention_diversity_index: attention_diversity, duration_ticks: consecutive_ticks_with_same_dominant_topic, active_goals_neglected: count(goals in goal_registry where goal.state == 'active' AND goal.description NOT semantically related to dominant_topic) }, suggested_remedy: 'Inject attention perturbation: temporarily boost salience for non-dominant topic features by +0.15 in next tick attention gate. If active_goals_neglected > 0, force goal-directed attention redirect to highest-priority neglected goal.' }. If active_goals_neglected > 2: escalate severity to 'high'. If attention_tunnel_effect detected for 20+ consecutive ticks: set metacognitive_flags.chronic_attention_tunnel = true for human review escalation. Log: { event: 'attention_tunnel_effect_check', diversity_index: attention_diversity, tunnel_detected: boolean, dominant_topic, tick_number }.
AnomalyDetection.step2_8: EMBODIED GWT INDICATOR PROPERTIES (v2.32.0 B-3): Compute consciousness indicator metrics based on Global Workspace Theory predictions, providing observable telemetry for GWT workspace health assessment. (1) WORKSPACE IGNITION RATE: Read perception_output.gwt_timing_metrics (from current tick's perception module output, passed via cognitive_state). Compute workspace_ignition_rate = gwt_timing_metrics.features_ignited / max(gwt_timing_metrics.feature_count_total, 1) over a 10-tick rolling window. Maintain ignition_rate_history in cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags (max 10 entries, FIFO). workspace_ignition_rate = mean(ignition_rate_history). If workspace_ignition_rate < 0.1 for 5+ consecutive ticks: flag { type: 'gwt_ignition_deficit', severity: 'medium', evidence: { ignition_rate: workspace_ignition_rate, history_window: 10, consecutive_low_ticks: N }, suggested_remedy: 'GWT workspace underperforming — broadcast threshold may be too high or broadcast_buffer too sparse. Consider reducing adaptive_ignition_threshold by 0.05 or increasing broadcast_priority_weights for reasoning/emotion modules.' }. (2) BROADCAST REACH RATIO: Compute broadcast_reach_ratio = count of modules that consumed at least one broadcast_buffer entry this tick / total_modules (8). Read from cognitive_state.broadcast_consumption_record (each module logs which broadcast entries it consumed). If broadcast_reach_ratio < 0.3 for 3+ consecutive ticks: flag { type: 'gwt_broadcast_isolation', severity: 'low', evidence: { reach_ratio: broadcast_reach_ratio, modules_reached: list, modules_silent: list }, suggested_remedy: 'Broadcast signals not reaching enough modules — check broadcast_buffer entry expiry and module consumption patterns.' }. (3) INFORMATION INTEGRATION (PHI PROXY): Compute information_integration_phi as a proxy for integrated information across modules. phi_proxy = Shannon mutual information between pairs of module outputs: I(perception; reasoning) + I(reasoning; decision) + I(emotion; decision) + I(metacognition; all). Approximate using output correlation: for each module pair, compute semantic_similarity of their primary outputs. phi_proxy = mean(pairwise_similarities) * module_diversity_factor, where module_diversity_factor = count(modules producing non-trivial output this tick) / total_modules. Clamp phi_proxy to [0.0, 1.0]. If phi_proxy < 0.2: flag { type: 'low_information_integration', severity: 'low', evidence: { phi_proxy, pairwise_details: [...], modules_active: N }, suggested_remedy: 'Cross-module integration weak — modules may be operating in isolation. Consider increasing broadcast_priority_weights or adding explicit cross-module data flow.' }. (4) OUTPUT: Record gwt_indicator_properties = { workspace_ignition_rate: float, broadcast_reach_ratio: float, information_integration_phi: float, gwt_health_composite: (0.4 * workspace_ignition_rate + 0.3 * broadcast_reach_ratio + 0.3 * information_integration_phi), tick_number } in metacognition_output for downstream consumption and observability dashboards. (5) LOG: { event: 'gwt_indicator_properties_computed', workspace_ignition_rate, broadcast_reach_ratio, phi_proxy, gwt_health_composite, tick_number }. Backward compatible: if gwt_timing_metrics is null (first tick or perception module not yet executed), skip computation and output gwt_indicator_properties = null.
AnomalyDetection.step3: For each detected anomaly: { anomaly_id, type, severity: 'low'|'medium'|'high', evidence, suggested_remedy }. Output anomalies_detected: [...]. High-severity anomalies trigger immediate strategy adjustments. Medium anomalies are logged for consolidation review. Low anomalies are noted but no action taken.
AnomalyDetection.constraints: (A) Anomaly detection must produce zero false claims -- only flag what is evidenced. (B) Maximum 5 anomalies per tick. (C) Each anomaly must cite specific evidence. (D) Perseveration detection requires at least 5 ticks of history. (E) GWT indicator properties (v2.32.0 B-3): workspace_ignition_rate and broadcast_reach_ratio use 10-tick rolling windows; phi_proxy clamped to [0.0, 1.0]; gwt_health_composite weighted formula is fixed (0.4/0.3/0.3).
AnomalyDetection.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(report no anomalies detected) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.

LearningExtraction.step1: [ASSERT] AnomalyDetection executed. If false -> go back to AnomalyDetection. | Extract learning signals from the current tick for consolidation. OUTCOME LEARNING: If action_result.success=true and decision_confidence was high: POSITIVE REINFORCEMENT -- strengthen association between current context and selected action. If action failed and decision_confidence was high: NEGATIVE SIGNAL -- flag overconfidence in this context.
LearningExtraction.step2: SCHEMA LEARNING: If reasoning produced novel inferences (not derivable from existing schema entries): candidate for schema_update during consolidation. Tag as { content, type: 'new_concept'|'new_relation'|'revision', source_tick, confidence }. EMOTIONAL LEARNING: If emotional prediction (appraisal-based emotion) matched actual outcome valence: calibration confirmed. If mismatch: candidate for emotional_model_update.
LearningExtraction.step2_5: INTRINSIC MOTIVATION SIGNAL (v1.4.0): Compute curiosity-driven exploration bonus using Intrinsic Curiosity Module principles (Pathak et al. 2017). (1) PREDICTION ERROR CURIOSITY: From perception module's prediction_error_report (v1.3.0), extract mean_prediction_error. curiosity_from_prediction = mean_prediction_error * 0.5 (novel stimuli trigger exploration). If prediction_error_report is null (not available), curiosity_from_prediction = 0.0. (2) KNOWLEDGE GAP CURIOSITY: Count hypotheses in reasoning_result with evidence_rating = 'insufficient'. knowledge_gap_count = count of insufficient-evidence hypotheses. curiosity_from_gaps = min(1.0, knowledge_gap_count * 0.25) (unresolved questions drive inquiry). (3) COMPETENCE SIGNAL: From confidence_calibration, if calibration_status = 'well_calibrated' AND reasoning_quality > 0.7: competence_satisfaction = 0.3 (mastery reward). Else: competence_satisfaction = 0.0. (4) COMPOSITE MOTIVATION: intrinsic_motivation = 0.4 * curiosity_from_prediction + 0.35 * curiosity_from_gaps + 0.25 * competence_satisfaction. Clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. COLD-START CURIOSITY (v1.4.1): If tick_number <= 3 AND long_term_entries count in schema.json < 5 (sparse knowledge state), inject cold_start_curiosity_bonus = 0.4 into intrinsic_motivation: intrinsic_motivation = max(intrinsic_motivation, cold_start_curiosity_bonus). This ensures early exploration when the agent has minimal prior knowledge, following the principle that sparse knowledge = high information gain potential (Schmidhuber 2010). Record cold_start_triggered: true in intrinsic_motivation_report. (5) MOTIVATION-DRIVEN LEARNING: If intrinsic_motivation > 0.5: add learning_signal { signal_type: 'curiosity_driven', content: 'High intrinsic motivation -- prioritize exploration and information-gathering actions', strength: intrinsic_motivation, source_tick: tick_number }. Additionally, set metacognitive_flags.exploration_bonus = intrinsic_motivation * 0.1 for Decision module to bias toward 'search' and 'recall' actions in next tick. EXPLORATION BONUS AUTO-ACTIVATION (v2.1.0 C-4): After computing action_diversity_index (from MetaCognitionOutput or current tick's performance_history), apply automatic exploration bonus regulation: (a) When action_diversity_index < 0.5 for 3+ consecutive ticks (tracked via cognitive_state.low_diversity_streak counter): auto-set metacognitive_flags.exploration_bonus = 0.05 to encourage action variety. Log { event: 'exploration_bonus_auto_activated', diversity_index: action_diversity_index, consecutive_low_ticks: low_diversity_streak }. (b) When mean(prediction_error_history last 5 entries) > 0.1 AND action_diversity_index > 0.7: reduce metacognitive_flags.exploration_bonus to 0.0 (high prediction error with good diversity means the agent is already exploring effectively and does not need artificial encouragement). Log { event: 'exploration_bonus_auto_deactivated', mean_prediction_error, diversity_index }. (6) Record intrinsic_motivation_report: { curiosity_from_prediction, curiosity_from_gaps, competence_satisfaction, intrinsic_motivation, exploration_bonus_set: boolean } in cognitive_state.motivation_history (rolling window, max 20 entries). Backward compatible: if prediction_error_report not available, rely on knowledge_gap and competence signals only.
LearningExtraction.step3: Compile learning_signals: [{ signal_type: 'reinforcement'|'schema_update'|'emotional_calibration'|'strategy_feedback', content, strength: float(0-1), source_tick }]. These signals are passed to Consolidation module for memory integration.
LearningExtraction.constraints: (A) Learning signals must be grounded in actual tick outcomes. (B) Maximum 10 learning signals per tick. (C) Schema update candidates require confidence > 0.6. (D) Emotional calibration signals require clear prediction-outcome comparison.
LearningExtraction.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(generate empty learning_signals array) -> inform(User). LOW.

ParameterTuning.step1: [ASSERT] LearningExtraction executed. If false -> go back to LearningExtraction. | MSI ROLLBACK COLD START INIT (v2.9.0 B-6): Before processing parameter adjustments, check for undefined MSI rollback state: if cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags.msi_rollback_log is undefined: cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags.msi_rollback_log = [], cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags.msi_composite_history = [], log { event: 'msi_rollback_init', reason: 'cold_start' }. This ensures MSI rollback references are always initialized before first use. SELF_MODEL_STATE SCHEMA VALIDATION (v2.23.0 QA-003 fix): Before consuming self_model_state, validate its schema if non-null: verify self_model_state contains { calibration_history: { entries: array, recent_accuracy: number }, reasoning_profile: { strengths: array, weaknesses: array }, strategy_history: array }. If any required sub-field is missing or has wrong type: log { event: 'self_model_schema_invalid', missing_fields: [...], action: 'reset_to_null' }, set self_model_state = null (treat as first run). This prevents downstream TypeError when ConfidenceCalibration.step2_5 or StrategyEvaluation.step3_6 access nested fields on a malformed self_model_state object. Apply adaptive parameter adjustments based on strategy evaluation and anomaly detection. For each strategy_adjustment from StrategyEvaluation: validate the suggested parameter change is within bounds (max 20% change). Apply if valid.
ParameterTuning.step2: ANOMALY-DRIVEN ADJUSTMENTS: For high-severity anomalies: (a) Circular reasoning -> reduce reasoning chain depth by 1. (b) Emotional override -> reduce emotional influence weight by 0.02. (c) Memory leak -> force decay of lowest-activation working memory slots. (d) Perseveration -> inject randomization factor (+0.1 exploration bonus to non-selected action types). (e) Fatigue cascade -> reduce cognitive load cap by 0.1. COGNITIVE LOAD ANOMALY DETECTION (v2.26.0 B-3): Cognitive load prediction uses 5-cycle sliding window for anomaly detection: compare current cognitive_load against mean of last 5 cycles; deviation > 2 standard deviations triggers COGNITIVE_LOAD_ANOMALY alert in metacognitive_report.
ParameterTuning.step2_5: 5D META-STATE INDEX (MSI) (v1.6.0): COMPUTE 5D META-STATE INDEX (MSI): msi_vector = { reasoning_quality: float(0-1) from ReasoningQualityAssess, confidence_calibration: float(0-1) from ConfidenceCalibration, strategy_effectiveness: float(0-1) from StrategyEvaluation, anomaly_severity: float(0-1) from AnomalyDetection (inverted: 1 - anomaly_score), learning_rate: float(0-1) from LearningExtraction, exploration_balance: float(0-1) —computed from perception's normalized_entropy: 1.0 if entropy in [0.3, 0.7] (balanced), lower if extreme exploration or exploitation }. Compute composite msi_score = weighted_mean(msi_vector, weights=[0.20, 0.20, 0.20, 0.15, 0.15, 0.10]). Include msi_vector and msi_score in metacognition output. Use msi_score for adaptive parameter scaling: if msi_score < 0.4, trigger conservative mode (reduce exploration, increase safety margins).
ParameterTuning.step2_6: ADJUSTMENT LOG & ROLLBACK (v1.6.0): (1) Before any parameter adjustment, snapshot current values as adjustment_log_entry: { tick, parameter_name, old_value, new_value, reason, msi_score_at_time }. Append to adjustment_log array (max 50 entries, FIFO eviction). (2) GRADIENT ROLLBACK (v2.24.0 B-3, replaces all-or-nothing rollback): If msi_score drops below 0.3 for 2 consecutive ticks after an adjustment, perform gradient-based selective rollback instead of blanket reversal. Specifically: identify the tick where MSI first dropped below 0.3 (stored in msi_decline_start_tick parameter; if null, use first adjustment_log entry with msi_score_at_time < 0.3). For each adjustment from that tick onward, compute rollback_priority = abs(msi_score_at_time - msi_score_current) * adjustment_magnitude where adjustment_magnitude = abs(new_value - old_value) / max(abs(old_value), 1e-8). Sort adjustments by rollback_priority descending. Rollback the top-N adjustments where N = ceil(total_candidate_adjustments * rollback_intensity), rollback_intensity = clamp((0.3 - msi_score) / 0.3, 0.2, 1.0). When msi_score=0.0 (worst case), rollback_intensity=1.0 (rollback all). When msi_score=0.24 (mild breach), rollback_intensity=0.2 (rollback only highest-impact 20%). Update msi_decline_start_tick: set to current tick when MSI first drops below 0.3 (was null), reset to null when MSI recovers above 0.4. Cap: never rollback more than 5 adjustments per tick to prevent cascading reversions. Set rollback_triggered = true and rollback_mode = 'gradient' in output. Log: { event: 'gradient_rollback', msi_score, rollback_intensity, candidates: total_candidate_adjustments, rolled_back: N }. (3) Write adjustment_log to {memory_dir}/metacognition_adjustments.json via file_system after each tuning pass. NOTE (v1.6.0): metacognition_adjustments.json is part of the memory/ directory architecture alongside schema.json, decay_config.json, and context_manager.json. Auto-created on first write if not present.
ParameterTuning.step2_7: COGNITIVE_LOAD_ADAPTIVE_THRESHOLD_LEARNING (v2.28.0 B-1): Replace fixed throttle/emergency_throttle thresholds with online learning mechanism. (1) HISTORY TRACKING: Read {memory_dir}/cognitive_load_thresholds.json via file_system. If not present, initialize: { throttle_threshold: 0.7, emergency_threshold: 0.9, load_history: [], learning_active: false, consecutive_emergency_count: 0, previous_thresholds: null }. (2) ACCUMULATE: Append current cognitive_state.cognitive_load_level to load_history (FIFO, max N=20 entries). (3) COLD START: If load_history.length < N (20 ticks not yet accumulated): use default thresholds (throttle=0.7, emergency=0.9), set learning_active=false. Log { event: 'adaptive_threshold_cold_start', samples: load_history.length, needed: 20, tick_number }. (4) ADAPTIVE COMPUTATION: When load_history.length >= N: compute mean_load = mean(load_history), std_load = std(load_history). throttle_threshold = mean_load + 1.5 * std_load. emergency_threshold = mean_load + 2.5 * std_load. (5) SAFETY FLOOR ENFORCEMENT: throttle_threshold = max(throttle_threshold, 0.6). emergency_threshold = max(emergency_threshold, 0.85). Ensure emergency_threshold > throttle_threshold (if not, set emergency_threshold = throttle_threshold + 0.15). Set learning_active=true. (6) ROLLBACK MECHANISM: If current cognitive_load_level > emergency_threshold: increment consecutive_emergency_count. If consecutive_emergency_count >= 3: revert to previous_thresholds (or defaults if null). Set learning_active=false, reset consecutive_emergency_count=0. Log { event: 'adaptive_threshold_rollback', reason: '3_consecutive_emergency_breaches', reverted_to: previous_thresholds | 'defaults', tick_number }. Reset load_history to [] to re-accumulate from clean state. If current cognitive_load_level <= emergency_threshold: reset consecutive_emergency_count=0. (7) PERSISTENCE: Before writing new thresholds, store current thresholds as previous_thresholds. Write updated { throttle_threshold, emergency_threshold, load_history, learning_active, consecutive_emergency_count, previous_thresholds } to {memory_dir}/cognitive_load_thresholds.json via file_system. (8) PROPAGATION: Set cognitive_state.adaptive_thresholds = { throttle: throttle_threshold, emergency: emergency_threshold, learning_active, samples: load_history.length } for downstream consumption by main.aisop.json cognitive load checks. Log { event: 'adaptive_threshold_update', throttle: throttle_threshold, emergency: emergency_threshold, mean_load, std_load, learning_active, tick_number }.
ParameterTuning.step3: Output parameter_updates: [{ parameter, old_value, new_value, trigger, effective_from: 'next_tick' }]. PARAMETER MODIFICATION AUDIT TRAIL (v2.13.0 B-4): For every parameter modification in parameter_updates, generate an immutable audit record: audit_entry = { audit_id: 'param_audit_{tick}_{index}', timestamp: ISO-8601 now, tick_number: current tick, who: { module: 'metacognition', function: 'ParameterTuning', trigger_source: strategy_adjustment.target_module | anomaly.type | 'msi_rollback' }, what: { parameter_name: parameter, old_value: old_value, new_value: new_value, change_magnitude: abs(new_value - old_value) / max(abs(old_value), 1e-8), change_direction: 'increase' | 'decrease' | 'reset' }, when: { cycle_count: cognitive_state.cycle_count, tick_number: tick_number, session_id: session_id, effective_from: 'next_tick' }, why: { trigger: strategy_adjustment.rationale | anomaly.suggested_remedy | 'msi_rollback_below_0.3', msi_score_at_time: msi_score, cognitive_health_at_time: overall_cognitive_health, supporting_evidence: [ anomaly.evidence | strategy_adjustment.evidence ] } }. Append audit_entry to cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags.parameter_audit_trail (rolling buffer, max 200 entries, FIFO eviction of oldest). AUDIT PERSISTENCE: Write audit_entry to {memory_dir}/parameter_audit_log.json via file_system (append mode, atomic write). If file does not exist, create with { version: '1.0.0', entries: [] }. AUDIT INTEGRITY: Compute SHA-256 hash of each audit_entry (excluding audit_hash field) and store as audit_entry.audit_hash. This enables tamper detection for the audit trail. ROLLBACK AUDIT: When MSI rollback is triggered (step2_6), generate additional audit entries with trigger='msi_rollback' for each rolled-back parameter, recording both the original adjustment and the rollback. IMMUTABLE PARAMETER AUDIT: For parameters marked as IMMUTABLE in constraints (safety thresholds, Axiom 0 weights), if any modification attempt is detected, generate audit_entry with { violation: true, severity: 'CRITICAL', parameter_name, attempted_change, blocked: true } and set metacognitive_flags.immutable_violation_alert = true. Log: { event: 'parameter_audit_trail_written', entries_count: len(new_audit_entries), total_trail_size: len(parameter_audit_trail), tick_number }. Write updated parameters to {memory_dir}/context_manager.json via file_system within the cognitive state parameter overrides section. Write updated self_model_state (merged calibration and strategy updates) to {memory_dir}/self_model.json via file_system using atomic write pattern (.tmp then rename). Create file on first write if absent (v2.15.0 B-3 self-model persistence).
ParameterTuning.constraints: (A) Parameter changes bounded to +/- 20% of current value. (B) Changes take effect next tick, not current. (C) Maximum 5 parameter changes per tick. (D) Critical parameters (safety thresholds, Axiom 0 weights) are IMMUTABLE -- never adjusted. (E) File writes use atomic pattern. (F) Parameter audit trail entries are immutable once written -- no retroactive modification of audit records (v2.13.0 B-4).
ParameterTuning.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(skip parameter tuning, retain current values) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.

MetaCognitionOutput.step1: [ASSERT] ParameterTuning executed. If false -> go back to ParameterTuning. | Compile complete metacognition output. ACTION DIVERSITY INDEX (v2.1.0 B-3): Compute action_diversity_index from performance_history. For each action_type in performance_history (last 20 entries): compute proportion p_i = count(action_type_i) / total_actions. Shannon entropy: H = -sum(p_i * log2(p_i)) for each action type. Normalized diversity_index = H / log2(N_types) where N_types = count of distinct action types used. Range [0, 1]: 0 = single type used exclusively, 1 = perfectly balanced across all types. If N_types <= 1: diversity_index = 0.0. Include action_diversity_index in metacognition_result output. METACOGNITIVE STATE VECTOR (v2.34.0 B-2): Compute 5-sensor metacognitive state vector as a formal structured self-assessment alongside the existing 4-dimension confidence_assessment. The 5 sensors provide complementary self-awareness dimensions: (1) emotional_awareness: float(0-1) = clamp(1.0 - abs(calibration_error) * 0.5 - (anomaly_count > 0 ? 0.1 * min(anomaly_count, 3) : 0), 0, 1). Measures the system's awareness of its own emotional state and its impact on processing. High emotional_awareness indicates accurate emotional self-monitoring. (2) correctness_evaluation: float(0-1) = reasoning_quality * 0.6 + (1.0 - calibration_error) * 0.4. Assesses the system's confidence in the correctness of its current reasoning outputs. Combines reasoning quality assessment with calibration accuracy. (3) experience_matching: float(0-1) = min(1.0, (self_model_state != null ? self_model_state.strategy_history.length / 100.0 : 0.0) * 0.5 + (performance_history.length / 20.0) * 0.5). Evaluates how well the current situation matches prior experience. Higher values indicate the system has encountered similar contexts before and can leverage learned patterns. (4) conflict_detection: float(0-1) = clamp(anomaly_severity_max * 0.4 + (strategy_adjustments.length / 3.0) * 0.3 + (msi_score < 0.4 ? 0.3 : 0.0), 0, 1), where anomaly_severity_max = max severity score among detected anomalies (high=1.0, medium=0.6, low=0.3, none=0.0). Detects internal conflicts between cognitive subsystems (e.g., emotional override vs reasoning, strategy disagreements, MSI degradation). (5) problem_importance: float(0-1) = clamp(relevance_proxy * 0.5 + goal_urgency_proxy * 0.3 + (primary_emotion_intensity > 0.5 ? 0.2 : 0.0), 0, 1), where relevance_proxy = max(action_result.success ? 0.6 : 0.8, decision_result.selected_action.confidence), goal_urgency_proxy = min(1.0, active_goal_count * 0.2). Estimates the importance of the current problem being processed, informing resource allocation decisions. Compute metacognitive_state_vector = { emotional_awareness, correctness_evaluation, experience_matching, conflict_detection, problem_importance, composite_self_assessment: mean([emotional_awareness, correctness_evaluation, experience_matching, conflict_detection, problem_importance]), tick_number }. Include metacognitive_state_vector in metacognition_result output. Log: { event: 'metacognitive_state_vector_computed', composite_self_assessment: float, sensors: { ea: emotional_awareness, ce: correctness_evaluation, em: experience_matching, cd: conflict_detection, pi: problem_importance }, tick_number }. Assemble metacognition_result: { confidence_assessment: { reasoning_quality, decision_quality: decision_confidence, emotional_calibration: calibration_error, overall_cognitive_health: weighted average }, strategy_adjustments: [...], anomalies_detected: [...], reflection_summary: string, learning_signals: [...], parameter_updates: [...], msi_vector: {...}, msi_score: float, action_diversity_index: float(0-1), metacognitive_state_vector: { emotional_awareness, correctness_evaluation, experience_matching, conflict_detection, problem_importance, composite_self_assessment, tick_number } }.
MetaCognitionOutput.step2: OVERALL COGNITIVE HEALTH: Compute overall_cognitive_health = 0.3 * reasoning_quality + 0.25 * (1 - calibration_error) + 0.25 * decision_confidence + 0.1 * (1 - fatigue_level) + 0.1 * (1 - anomaly_count/5). Clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. If health < 0.4: flag 'cognitive_degradation' -- recommend sleep/consolidation. METACOGNITIVE SENSITIVITY (v1.3.0): After computing confidence_assessment, calculate metacognitive_sensitivity_index (MSI_AUC): (1) Maintain a rolling calibration_history in cognitive_state.metacognitive_flags.calibration_history (last 50 ticks): [{ tick, predicted_confidence, actual_outcome_quality }]. (2) Compute MSI_AUC = AUC of ROC curve where predicted_confidence is the score and actual_outcome_quality > 0.7 is the positive label. If calibration_history.length < 10, set MSI_AUC = null (insufficient data). (3) If MSI_AUC < 0.6 (poor calibration): flag metacognitive_flags.calibration_alert = true, add to anomalies_detected: { type: 'poor_metacognitive_calibration', severity: 'HIGH', msi_auc_value: MSI_AUC, recommendation: 'Confidence scores are unreliable -- increase reasoning depth or request human verification' }. HUMAN ESCALATION PROTOCOL (v1.3.0): If confidence_assessment.overall_cognitive_health < 0.4 OR (decision_quality < 0.3 AND reasoning_quality < 0.3): set metacognitive_flags.human_escalation_required = true, add strategy_adjustment: { target_module: 'decision', adjustment: 'defer_to_human', rationale: 'Cognitive health critically low -- human oversight required per Axiom 0' }. The escalation flag is consumed by Decision module in next tick to present options to user instead of autonomous action.
MetaCognitionOutput.step2_5: METACOGNITIVE STATE VECTOR EXPORT (v2.35.0 B-3): After computing metacognitive_state_vector and overall cognitive health, export a structured state vector snapshot for cross-session analytics and external monitoring. (1) STATE VECTOR SERIALIZATION: Construct exportable state_vector_export = { schema_version: '1.0', session_id: cognitive_state.session_id, tick_number: current_tick, timestamp: current_timestamp, sensors: { emotional_awareness: metacognitive_state_vector.emotional_awareness, correctness_evaluation: metacognitive_state_vector.correctness_evaluation, experience_matching: metacognitive_state_vector.experience_matching, conflict_detection: metacognitive_state_vector.conflict_detection, problem_importance: metacognitive_state_vector.problem_importance }, composite_self_assessment: metacognitive_state_vector.composite_self_assessment, cognitive_health: overall_cognitive_health, msi_score: msi_score, anomaly_summary: { count: anomalies_detected.length, max_severity: max(anomalies_detected[].severity) or 'none', types: unique(anomalies_detected[].type) }, strategy_summary: { adjustments_count: strategy_adjustments.length, target_modules: unique(strategy_adjustments[].target_module) }, action_diversity_index: action_diversity_index, calibration_error: calibration_error }. (2) PERSISTENCE: Write state_vector_export to {memory_dir}/metacognitive_state_history.json via file_system (append mode, max 200 entries with FIFO eviction). Use atomic write pattern (.tmp then rename). (3) CROSS-SESSION ANALYTICS SUPPORT: If metacognitive_state_history.json has >= 10 entries: compute rolling statistics: { avg_composite_self_assessment_10: mean(last 10 composite_self_assessment), trend_composite: linear_slope(last 10 composite_self_assessment), sensor_stability: { per_sensor_variance over last 10 entries }, cognitive_health_trend: linear_slope(last 10 cognitive_health) }. Include rolling_analytics in state_vector_export output. This enables external monitoring systems and cross-session dashboards to consume structured metacognitive telemetry without parsing full metacognition_result objects. (4) LOG: { event: 'metacognitive_state_vector_exported', composite_self_assessment, cognitive_health, history_size: entries_in_file, tick_number }.
MetaCognitionOutput.step2_6: MSV CROSS-SESSION PERSISTENCE EMIT (v2.36.0 B4; baseline H-1, ref arXiv 2603.07670 / arXiv 2603.11768 SSGM cross-session identity): Beyond the intra-session metacognitive_state_history.json telemetry (step2_5, max 200 FIFO), EMIT a cross-session MSV-persistence record so the metacognitive state vector survives across sessions and can warm-start a new session. metacognition does NOT write memory directly here (consolidation owns the memory write/read authority — see consolidation.ConsolidationOutput v2.36.0 B4); instead set metacognition_result.msv_persistence_emit = { schema_version: '1.0', timestamp: current_timestamp, tick_number: current_tick, session_id: cognitive_state.session_id, user_id: cognitive_state.user_id (may be null), identity_key: (cognitive_state.user_id != null ? cognitive_state.user_id : cognitive_state.session_id), msv: { emotional_awareness, correctness_evaluation, experience_matching, conflict_detection, problem_importance, composite_self_assessment }, cognitive_health: overall_cognitive_health }. IDENTITY NOTE: cross-session identity resolution is an OPEN PROBLEM — if user_id is null, mark scope='session_local' so consolidation does NOT use it for cross-session warm-start. CONTRADICTION/ROLLBACK SIGNAL: if a prior MSV is available in cognitive_state.msv_warm_start AND abs(composite_self_assessment - msv_warm_start.composite_self_assessment) > 0.5, set msv_persistence_emit.rollback_candidate = true (consolidation flags it; a poisoned/corrupted MSV trajectory can be rolled back to the last known-good entry). Log: { event: 'msv_persistence_emitted', identity_scope: ('cross_session' if user_id else 'session_local'), rollback_candidate: boolean, tick_number }.
MetaCognitionOutput.step3: REFLECTION SUMMARY: Generate human-readable reflection: 'Tick [N]: [action_taken] with [confidence] confidence. Reasoning quality: [grade]. [anomaly_count] anomalies detected. [adjustment_count] strategy adjustments recommended. Cognitive health: [health_score]. MSI: [msi_score].' Return metacognition_result to main.aisop.json caller.
MetaCognitionOutput.constraints: (A) Output must be complete with all assessment dimensions. (B) Reflection summary must be honest and concise (max 300 characters). (C) Cognitive health below 0.4 must always trigger degradation flag. (D) All numeric fields in valid ranges. (E) metacognitive_state_vector: all 5 sensors must be present and clamped to [0.0, 1.0]; composite_self_assessment is the arithmetic mean of all 5 sensors (v2.34.0 B-2). (F) state_vector_export MUST be written to metacognitive_state_history.json on every tick using atomic write pattern; max 200 entries FIFO (v2.35.0 B-3). (G) Cross-session rolling analytics require minimum 10 history entries; output rolling_analytics = null if fewer (v2.35.0 B-3). (H) PERSISTENCE PATH VERIFICATION (v2.35.0 QS-3): state_vector_export persistence write-path MUST include all v2.35.0 exported fields: sensors (5 dimensions), composite_self_assessment, cognitive_health, msi_score, anomaly_summary, strategy_summary, action_diversity_index, calibration_error, and rolling_analytics (when available). Verify {memory_dir}/metacognitive_state_history.json write succeeds before returning; on write failure, set metacognitive_flags.state_vector_export_failed = true and include state_vector_export in cognitive_state.error_context for recovery. context_manager.json MUST also reflect the latest metacognitive_state_vector in cognitive_state for cross-session continuity.
MetaCognitionOutput.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(return minimal output with reflection_summary only) -> inform(User). LOW.
